posts.text:
A while ago I was trying to sell CrewAI to a huge bank.

They liked the platform. Then they asked how they would do observability, and I had to say they would need to buy something else.

Then memory. Same answer.

By the third answer they were sitting there thinking, alright, I have to buy five products to use yours.

That meeting ended an argument we had been having internally for months.

Everyone can tell you the stack is fragmenting. Data, models, orchestration, observability, connection, interface. Every layer pulling in companies who want to own exactly one thing.

Sit on the other side of the table and it flips.

Nobody wants five contracts. Five security reviews. Five vendors to chase at 2am. They want one number to call.

So what do you do when the market pulls apart and the buyer pulls together?

You build the boring parts anyway. Deployment, traces, PII, permissions, the governance a bank asks about first.

Architecture arguments get settled by procurement. Not by engineers.

posts.translationZh:
前阵子我想把 CrewAI 卖给一家大型银行。

他们喜欢这个平台。然后他们问可观测性怎么做，我只能说他们还需要买别的东西。

接着问记忆。答案一样。

到第三个问题时，他们坐在那里想：好吧，用你们的产品还得再买五个产品。

那次会议结束了我们内部持续数月的一场争论。

所有人都能告诉你，技术栈正在碎片化。数据、模型、编排、可观测性、连接、界面。每一层都在吸引那些只想占住其中一件事的公司。

但坐到桌子的另一边，情况就反过来了。

没人想要五份合同。五次安全审查。五个凌晨 2 点要追的供应商。他们只想要一个能拨通的号码。

那么，当市场在拆分、买方却在整合时，你该怎么办？

你还是要把那些无聊的部分做出来。部署、链路追踪、PII、权限，以及银行最先会问到的治理。

架构争论最终由采购决定。不是工程师。

π-0.7 API hackathon
where we learn that in fact an excavator and a nerf gun are also robots

kudos to @ActorLabs for the awesome event

quotedTweet.text:
Over the weekend, I put an unreleased checkpoint of π0.7 inside an excavator and placed 2nd at the @ActorLabs + @physical_int  36hr hackathon.

With about an hour of embodied data (3 cameras and joystick values, no joint angles), the policy could continuously move dirt with a single prompt.

This was so straightforward to get working (pi is cooking) we spent the rest of the hackathon mounting a Nerf minigun on the roof. We added a people searching/tracking + firing feature to prevent people from getting too close to the dangerous machinery (ai safety feature).

Here’s how we built it + more details (data collection, hardware hax, sim2real, video of me getting shot)🧵
quotedTweet.translationZh:
周末，我把 π0.7 的一个未发布 checkpoint 装进了一台挖掘机，并在 @ActorLabs + @physical_int 36 小时黑客松中获得第 2 名。

只用了大约一小时的具身数据（3 个摄像头和摇杆数值，没有关节角度），这个策略就能通过一个提示词持续铲土。

让它跑起来非常顺利（pi 正在起飞），所以黑客松剩下的时间我们都用来把一挺 Nerf 迷你机枪装到车顶上。我们加入了寻找/追踪人员并开火的功能，防止人们靠近危险机械（AI 安全功能）。

这是我们的搭建过程和更多细节（数据采集、硬件魔改、sim2real、我被射中的视频）🧵

quotedTweet.text:
Introducing Praxis-1, an open-weight World Action Model that turns our video pre-training expertise into real world control for robots.

Robot demonstration data is limited. But video data is infinite. Praxis-1 extends our bet that the best policy models will learn from video, and use that scale to bring embodied intelligence to every industry.

Praxis-1 is built on our large-scale video pre-training and real-time infrastructure, and acts as a policy model for robotics developers and researchers that works across any embodiment or environment, no matter how complex.

We are actively testing with early partners including Noble Machines, Standard Bots and Ultra, and will be releasing the weights publicly in the coming months.

Learn more and request early access at https://t.co/DzCMQpYNXQ

机器人演示数据有限，但视频数据近乎无限。Praxis-1 延续了我们的判断：最好的策略模型将从视频中学习，并利用这种规模化能力，把具身智能带到每个行业。

Praxis-1 基于我们的大规模视频预训练和实时基础设施构建，可作为机器人开发者和研究人员使用的策略模型，适用于任何形态或环境，无论多么复杂。

quotedTweet.text:
🎉 Introducing Databricks AI Decide: make fast decisions on your governed data

Following the TypeSafe AI Jev launch, we’ve seen increasing demand for a fast, low-cost API that turns raw text into structured decisions. However, many of our enterprise customers are unable to use Jev due to data privacy and access concerns.

AI Decide is our enterprise-grade function for fast decisions on customer’s governed data. It is supported for batch use cases like processing millions of documents with SQL and for realtime applications like model routing through our REST API. Starting early next week, customers will also be able to govern permissions on the ai_decide function through Databricks Unity Gateway.

A big shoutout to @mattydtweetz @ivanzhouyq @nihit_desai @hanlintang for getting this new function launched in less than a week!

How many people show up on a Tuesday night to talk about document processing for AI agents? 🤔

In New York, enough to fill the room and start a waitlist. In San Francisco, almost 600.

We were in both cities on the same night to talk about one problem: agents don't read documents the way people do. Look at an invoice and you can tell the monthly rate from the total in a second. An agent often gets the words without the layout, so it has to guess.

In New York, we partnered with @usekernel on @braintrust's Agent Builders Night. In San Francisco, we partnered with @WorkOS on @daytonaio's AI Builders event. Thanks to them for having us, and to Abrar and Yong from our team for speaking!

reviewedPosts.author: joaomdmoura
reviewedPosts.text:
A while ago I was trying to sell CrewAI to a huge bank.

They liked the platform. Then they asked how they would do observability, and I had to say they would need to buy something else.

Then memory. Same answer.

By the third answer they were sitting there thinking, alright, I have to buy five products to use yours.

That meeting ended an argument we had been having internally for months.

Everyone can tell you the stack is fragmenting. Data, models, orchestration, observability, connection, interface. Every layer pulling in companies who want to own exactly one thing.

Sit on the other side of the table and it flips.

Nobody wants five contracts. Five security reviews. Five vendors to chase at 2am. They want one number to call.

So what do you do when the market pulls apart and the buyer pulls together?

You build the boring parts anyway. Deployment, traces, PII, permissions, the governance a bank asks about first.

Architecture arguments get settled by procurement. Not by engineers.
